minutes.headline: Select Board backed the pavement plan restored via cuts and a majority refused to put any override on the ballot.
minutes.summary: The board reviewed the town manager's balanced FY26 omnibus budget, including how the pavement management plan was restored through cuts elsewhere, and found a percent-change error for the schools. Members then discussed a citizen-petition school override and a possible town override; a majority said they would not support putting either on the ballot. No formal budget or override vote was taken; the warrant article vote was pushed to a later meeting.

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comment; none on site or Zoom at first.
Complimented the finance staff member and urged that the cemetery expansion request not be funded, saying plots are already available.
Responded on the cemetery expansion and the grant writing services line, saying procedures for using it were never set up.
Said the board's override arguments repeat last year's, noted the school committee's public vote that it does not need more funding, and hoped for solutions next year.
Asked whether the restored pavement management plan includes a contribution to OPEB; answered yes.

budget_items.what_was_said: Two budget versions were presented, one with the plan restored and one without it.
Overlay was decreased, adding revenue, which rebalanced the sheets.
Snow and ice level funded, grant writer position removed, police overtime cut, reserve fund and other lines reduced.
Taxation support for capital reduced and replaced with free cash.
Reserve reduced as the pay plan adjustment was dropped and the library director salary was set.
An additional position was not included; extra float hours were added.
Members found the change column used the original appropriation rather than the revised budget, so the school change was corrected.

budget_items.topic: Total dollar change on last page
budget_items.what_was_said: Bottom change calculation would be updated but not the budget totals.
An IT manager role was shifted to a contracted line, raising that line.
Board discussed taking more free cash to give the schools; a special education move-in might be absorbed by the schools.
Debate on whether to buy trucks with Chapter 90 funds given the reduced pavement plan.
Accounts payable and payroll warrants were read.
A resident argued the expansion is unnecessary.

decisions.decision: Board members indicated they were comfortable with the town manager's restoration of the pavement management plan and the cuts used to fund it.
Vote on placing an override on the ballot deferred to a later agenda; the board would meet April 1.
A majority of the board said it would not support a town or school override on the ballot this year.

what_happened.line: A majority of the Select Board said it would not support putting a town or school override on the ballot this year.
No formal budget or override vote was taken; the vote on placing an override on the ballot was deferred to the April 1 meeting.
Board members indicated they were comfortable with the town manager restoring the pavement management plan through cuts to other lines.
Members found the school percent change used the original appropriation rather than the revised budget, and the school change was corrected.
The board discussed giving the schools more free cash, and debated buying DPW trucks with Chapter 90 funds given the reduced pavement plan.

why_it_matters: Without an override on the ballot, the FY26 budget would have to balance within the levy limit, so any school or town needs beyond it would depend on free cash and cuts rather than a tax vote.
The pavement plan was kept by cutting or reducing other lines, such as police overtime, the reserve fund and a grant writer position, so road funding and those services are linked in this budget.
